source.title: SAMPLE COSTS TO ESTABLISH AN ORCHARD AND PRODUCE
source.counties: Kathrine S. Pope Farm Advisor, UC Cooperative Extension, Yolo
source.description: Establish and produce an orchard, micro-sprinkler irrigation
source.publisher: UC Davis Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics / UC Cooperative Extension

priceYear.quote: The costs are based on January 2016, Energy Information Administration (EIA), monthly data.

acresFarmed.quote: The hypothetical farm consists of 105 contiguous acres farmed by the owner.

acresCrop.quote: Almonds are being established on 100 acres; roads, irrigation systems and farmstead occupy five acres.

interestRatePct.quote: An interest rate of 3.25 percent is used to calculate capital recovery.

operatingInterestRatePct.quote: Interest on operating capital is based on cash operating costs and is calculated monthly until harvest at a nominal rate of 4.25 percent per year.

laborMachineRate.quote: Hourly wages for workers are $14.00 for machine operators and $12.00 per hour non-machine labor.

laborNonMachineRate.quote: Hourly wages for workers are $14.00 for machine operators and $12.00 per hour non-machine labor.

fuelPriceDiesel.quote: Prices for on-farm delivery of diesel and gasoline are $2.49 and $2.77 per gallon, respectively.

fuelPriceGas.quote: Prices for on-farm delivery of diesel and gasoline are $2.49 and $2.77 per gallon, respectively.

costsPerAcre.title: COSTS PER ACRE TO PRODUCE ALMONDS

capitalRecoveryFormula.quote: The formula for the calculation of the annual capital recovery costs is ((Purchase Price – Salvage Value) x Capital Recovery Factor) + (Salvage Value x Interest Rate).

salvageMethod.quote: Salvage value is an estimate of the remaining value of an investment at the end of its useful life.

propertyTaxRatePct.quote: For this study, county taxes are calculated as 1 percent of the average value of the property.

machineLaborFactor.quote: Labor time for operations involving machinery is 20 percent higher than the equipment time to account for the extra labor involved in equipment set up, moving, maintenance, work breaks, and field repair.
